key_insight: VeriFine shows how to scale verification itself so embodied agents can keep improving as they encounter new failure modes. Instead of relying on a fixed judge, it adapts verification to match the evolving abilities of the policy.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the bottleneck in self-improving embodied AI where static evaluators cannot reliably judge new behaviors, limiting both training feedback and the discovery of useful examples. This is especially difficult in embodied reasoning, where evaluation must account for spatial grounding, causality, and safety.
method: Introduces VeriFine, an agent harness framework that scales verification alongside self-improvement.
Uses verification that can adapt to newly emerging failure patterns rather than staying fixed.
Targets embodied reasoning tasks where judgments must combine correctness, grounding, and safety-aware decisions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes self-improvement loops more reliable and scalable by improving the quality of feedback and training data selection. It is especially useful for building embodied agents that need to operate safely and reason about the physical world.

paper_title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning
paper_authors: Zewei Zhou, Rachel Luo, Yulong Cao, Chaowei Xiao, Chensheng Peng
